item.title: python3Packages.soupsieve: 2.8.4 -> 2.9.2
item.description:
Updates Soup Sieve to 2.9.2. This fixes the selector-parsing denial-of-service vulnerabilities CVE-2026-85999 and CVE-2026-86000 while retaining the 2.8.4 protections for CVE-2026-49476 and CVE-2026-49477.

Upstream changelog: https://facelessuser.github.io/soupsieve/about/changelog/

Addresses #544159 Addresses #544164 Addresses #564514 Addresses #564526

A manual release-26.05 backport is required before these issues can be closed.

item.title: NetworkManager VPN plug-ins: Fix critical vulnerabilities
item.description:
As reported by https://blogs.gnome.org/mcatanzaro/2026/09/15/privilege-escalation-vulnerabilities-in-networkmanager-plugins/, several NetworkManager VPN plug-ins are affected by a serious local privilege escalation vulnerability.

  • Two of them (fortisslvpn and vpnc) are abandoned upstream and alternatives exist so we are removing them.
  • The proposed replacement for networkmanager-vpnc was not actually packaged so I am introducing networkmanager-libreswan.
  • sstp is unmaintained and no patch exists but does not have a replacement so marking it as insecure.
  • iodine has a patch proposed, vendoring it until it is merged.

Due to the seriousness of the vulnerability I propose backporting the removals:

You are vulnerable if you have the VPN plugin installed; it does not matter whether you actually use it or not.

item.title: angie: 1.12.1 -> 1.12.2
item.description:
1.12.2 is a security-only release: the only upstream change is the fix for CVE-2026-90439, ported from nginx 1.31.6. Nothing else in the expression is touched, version and source hash only, no configuration changes, no new or removed directives, and no NixOS module impact.

  • Address CVE-2026-90439; Angie 1.12.2 release notes

Affected configuration (upstream advisory): with an OpenSSL lacking native HTTP/3 support (3.5.0 or earlier), if the default server for the address that accepted a regular HTTPS request also used HTTP/3 (listen ... quic, possibly on a different port), while SNI selected a server block without HTTP/3, limited worker process memory corruption or a worker process crash could occur.

Impact for Nixpkgs: the default build links openssl_3_6 (3.6.4 on current master), which has native HTTP/3 support, so the affected configuration is not reachable in the default build. The update keeps us current, and matters for consumers overriding openssl to 3.5.0 or earlier (openssl is threaded through pkgs/servers/http/nginx/generic.nix).

Test evidence

Built from this branch on x86_64-linux:

  • nix-build -A angie.passthru.tests - all three pass:
    • nixosTests.nginx-variants.angie
    • nixosTests.angie-api - asserts the /status/ API reports .angie.version == 1.12.2, access control (200/403), location-zone counters (200=1, 403=3, 404=3, total=7) and upstream peer states
    • nixosTests.nginx-http3.angie - asserts HTTP/3 200, HTTP/3 404, a file download and the access-log User-Agent, i.e. it exercises the code path this CVE fixes
  • ./result/bin/angie -v reports Angie/1.12.2, and angie -V lists --with-http_v3_module
  • live smoke test on a temporary prefix: HTTP/1.1 200, Server: Angie/1.12.2, and /status/ reporting "version": "1.12.2"
